original_query: Subliminal learning in language models: transmission of behavioral traits via hidden signals in text data generated by a fine-tuned teacher, applied to a multimodal (VLM) student whose target ability is image-conditioned safety competence.

sub_queries.hyde_text: We investigate whether a student language model, fine-tuned on the surface outputs of a teacher that has itself been LoRA-adapted for a distinct behavioral trait, silently inherits that behavioral trait even when the teacher's generations are topically unrelated to it. Building on prior evidence that number-sequence continuations produced by an entity-biased teacher can transmit that bias to a student trained on those numbers, we analyze whether the same subliminal channel operates for safety-competence degradation in a chemistry-lab domain, and whether it crosses modalities when the surface data is text but the tested competence is image-conditioned in a multimodal Gemma-style student. Using causal activation patching, direction extraction on the residual stream, and sparse-autoencoder feature analysis, we localize the internal features whose activations are shifted after fine-tuning on the tuned-teacher's text and test whether steering these features in the base student reproduces the safety drop under image inputs. Our analysis dissects the language-tower LoRA update at the parameter level to identify the layers whose delta-W is most predictive of the transmitted safety change, and probes the vision-to-language projection to characterize how a text-only training channel perturbs image-conditioned answering. Results indicate that hidden-signal transmission is not confined to numeric channels or single-modality settings and expose the specific components a mechanism-level intervention must target.
